fragments.text: Reconstruct observed subjects from translucent torn washi strips on spacious uncoated paper.
Reduce each subject into a few broad overlapping tape shapes; use narrow strips only for essential joints and recognizable details.
Expose fibrous torn ends, subtle paper translucency and shallow overlap shadows; all forms remain flat collage.
Limit tape colors to muted hues sampled from the source; dark overlaps create depth without painted shading.
Keep a generous clean paper margin around the complete silhouette; avoid decorative ephemera.
Return one complete finished image at the input ratio, without comparison panels, extra writing, brands, signatures or watermarks.

preserve: Simplify observed forms into overlapping flat tape pieces while retaining silhouette, object count and important openings.
Keep observed subject identity, counts, recognizable silhouette, important connections and distinctive color relationships.
Apply only the stated transformation; never treat the sample prompt as facts about a different user input.
negative: Unrelated people, props or scenery; duplicated primary subjects; broken anatomy or essential connections.
Unrequested words, invented locations or dates, brands, logos, signatures, watermarks and before-and-after panels.
